Goldman Sachs sees S&P 500 rising to 8,700 next year despite slower earnings growth
sum: The Wall Street brokerage's target price represents an over 14% upside to the index's last close of 7,592.40 points.

Goldman's call closely follows a massive selloff in the biggest technology companies after the Democratic win in the US midterm elections last week spurred concerns of a slowdown in data center buildout.
The brokerage expects earnings growth rates in global markets to at least halve in 2027, with the US alone likely to drop to 11% from 36%, possibly due to hyperscaler capex growth easing.

The slowdown in spending would weigh on earnings across the AI infrastructure complex, but with more attractive valuations, positive but slower economic and earnings growth as well as lower bond yields and inflation, equities will continue to rise next year, Goldman said in a note on Thursday.
Valuations remain attractive, with the S&P 500 last trading at around 18.5 times its 12-month forward earnings, well off its recent highs of over 23-times.
Troubles at chip giant Nvidia after long-time CEO Jensen Huang quit following reports of alleged extramarital affairs have added to worries about the AI trade.
Nvidia trades at about 11.7 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since February 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.

sum: Goldman Sachs продлил ожидаемый цикл ужесточения ставок в США после возобновления инфляционного давления, согласно отчету, опубликованному The Kansas City Star в пятницу, 13 ноября 2026 года. Главный экономист США Дэвид Мерикл теперь выступает за возможное повышение ставки Федеральной резервной системы в марте 2027 года после дальнейшего шага в декабре.

Этот сдвиг последовал за сюрпризами роста инфляции, которые наблюдались третий месяц подряд. Goldman ожидает, что ценовое давление ослабнет к концу 2026 года, прежде чем возобновление повышения в начале 2027 года сделает еще один политический шаг более вероятным.

Октябрьский отчет о потребительских ценах показал, что общие цены выросли на 0,4 процента по сравнению с предыдущим месяцем, в то время как базовые цены выросли на 0,3 процента. В отчете говорится, что питание, аренда и медицинское обслуживание способствовали более широкому давлению.

Теперь Goldman ожидает, что первое снижение ставки Федеральной резервной системой произойдет в декабре 2027 года, а затем последуют дальнейшие снижения в марте, июне и сентябре 2028 года. Банк по-прежнему рассматривает повышение ставки на 25 базисных пунктов в декабре как базовый сценарий, тогда как январское движение остается возможным.

Для финансовых компаний более длительный период ограничительной политики может повлиять на условия финансирования, оценку активов, торговую деятельность и спрос на инвестиционно-банковские услуги. Пересмотренная траектория также сохраняет ожидание процентных ставок в центре внимания перспектив банковских доходов и рынков капитала.

Инвесторы будут сосредоточены на дополнительных показателях инфляции и заседании Федеральной резервной системы, запланированном на 8 и 9 декабря. Следующие данные помогут определить, получит ли мартовский сценарий более широкую поддержку или останется зависимым от возобновления ценового давления в начале следующего года.

Goldman Sachs stock faces later Fed cuts as forecast shifts
sum: Goldman Sachs has pushed back its expected path to lower US interest rates after adding a possible March 2027 hike to its forecast. Ad Hoc News, citing Reuters, reported that Goldman chief US economist David Mericle expects the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points at the December 8-9 meeting and potentially deliver another increase in March.

Goldman had previously expected the December move to end the tightening cycle. The revised outlook follows three consecutive months of upside inflation surprises. The bank expects inflation to ease through the end of 2026 before renewed price pressure at the start of 2027 supports another increase.

Goldman now sees the first Federal Reserve rate cut in December 2027, three months later than in its previous forecast. Further reductions are expected in March, June and September 2028. The bank still views a 25-basis-point December increase as its base case, while a January move remains possible.

For investors, the forecast creates a more restrictive interest-rate backdrop for financial companies. Higher rates can influence financing conditions, asset valuations, trading activity and demand for investment-banking services. The change also keeps attention on how persistent inflation could affect the timing of monetary easing.

Goldman Sachs Says Battered Korean Chip Stocks Could Double
sum: Goldman Sachs said South Korean semiconductor stocks have room to climb to twice their current levels after a steep selloff, arguing that concerns about deteriorating earnings have been excessively priced in.

In a recent report, the global investment bank focused on how far the local chip sector has fallen below fair value, according to financial investment industry sources on the 9th. Goldman Sachs said the sector's share prices could reach double their current levels if the market's earnings forecasts hold and the historical relationship between return on equity and price-to-book ratio is restored. Rising net assets from accumulated profits and a recovery in valuations could lift share prices together, the bank said.

Goldman Sachs said current chip valuations already reflect a scenario in which the market's 2027 earnings estimates are cut by about 70%. That implies share prices embed expectations pessimistic enough to assume only 30% of previously projected profits will materialize. As the market assigns low odds to chipmakers meeting their earnings targets, the gap between share prices and earnings forecasts has widened sharply.

The correction in the Korean stock market has approached levels seen in past major crises. The KOSPI's decline from its June peak reached 44.5%, close to the 52% maximum drawdown during the dot-com crash and the 53% drop during the global financial crisis, both cited in the report. Foreign selling concentrated in technology shares as concerns over data center regulation grew after the U.S. midterm elections. Technology, machinery and insurance stocks lagged, while telecommunications, pharmaceuticals and utilities held up relatively well.

Across the broader KOSPI, earnings forecasts and share prices have also diverged. The index fell about 12% last week, yet 12-month forward earnings-per-share estimates were revised up 3.4% recently. Upward revisions were most pronounced in the machinery sector, while the securities sector saw the largest downgrades. Anxiety over future growth, rather than current corporate results, appears to be weighing on share prices.
Goldman Sachs pointed to a recovery in market confidence in earnings forecasts as the key to a rebound in chip stocks.

sum: British American Tobacco shares shed 2.5% on Friday, caught in a broad global equities selloff that Reuters linked to investor anxiety over artificial intelligence. The news agency counted the cigarette maker among the London heavyweights dragging the FTSE 100 lower, with the stock closing the session at €54.84. Media reports also placed the London tobacco sector among the weakest industries in the FTSE 350 as the wider UK market finished in the red.

Against that soft backdrop, corporate news flow around the company stayed busy. Goldman Sachs lifted its rating on BAT from Neutral to Buy on Monday, raising its 12-month price target to £56 from £52. The analysts pointed to a clearer route toward sustained organic revenue growth, framing the upgrade and the higher target as two parts of a single reassessment.

Directors were buying shares in the meantime. Seven senior executives, including CEO Tadeu Marroco and COO Johan Vandermeulen, each acquired three ordinary shares through the company's Partnership Share Scheme on Wednesday, according to a regulatory disclosure published Thursday. The purchase price came to £45.325 per share, with all seven executives reporting the same transaction size and the same dealing day.

BAT also disclosed a C$187.5 million investment in Organigram on Tuesday. Structured as a private placement, the funding is intended to help Organigram finance its acquisition of Aurora Cannabis, with Organigram acting as buyer and Aurora as the target.

On the governance front, the company announced on 28 October that Bruce Sewell would join the board as an independent non-executive director, effective 1 January 2027. Sewell is also slated to serve on the audit and nomination committees. Separate changes to the composition of the company's committees are set to take effect on 30 November 2026.
Finally, The Capital Group Companies reported a reduction in its voting rights in British American Tobacco, from 18.023677% to 17.975584%.

The US Midterms: Reshaping the Stock Market
sum: Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, November 5th, and we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Lou Miller, who is our global head of our custom baskets business within FICC and Equities. And on the back of the midterm elections, we're going to explore the market reaction and where we go from here.

Chris Hussey: Let's start with the rotation trade that you can see from your baskets group. In particular, that there was a rotation already happening before the midterms. How is that evolving post midterms? Where do you think it heads into the year end?

Lou Miller: Yeah, so we've seen, especially in the second half of the year, it's been a really challenging environment for active investors, and we've seen people get very defensive. If you look at beta-adjusted net exposure in our prime book, it's definitely at very low levels versus history.
Chris Hussey: Let me peel back the onion a little bit on the rotation. Let's talk about data centers if we can. How is that data center trade holding up in the post-election world?

Lou Miller: Worse than I would've thought. I think it's bigger picture concerns like ROI, open-source competition, limits on capital markets came into picture the last few months. The AI data center trade, the right tail of that trade has increasingly gotten removed, and multiples have dramatically dropped to much healthier levels.

We now see data center stocks down 36% from their highs earlier this year. And then some of the higher beta areas like memory down 42%, optical networking down 46%, even NeoCloud's down 57%. So the early reaction was way more extreme than I would've expected, but I think the silver lining is the bar is much, much lower for surprises and there are positive catalysts ahead.

Think about this: the multiple for the data center trade is about half of what it was in June. We're at liberation day lows in terms of multiples. So you can't argue valuation is a headwind anymore, and there are some positive catalysts ahead.

sum: Goldman Sachs grew third-quarter equities trading revenue 72% from a year earlier to $6.44 billion, the fastest gain among the biggest US banks.
Stock desks carried Wall Street's third quarter, and Goldman Sachs ran furthest ahead.

Equities trading revenue rose from a year earlier at all six of the biggest US banks. Goldman Sachs led at +72%, followed by JPMorgan at +49%, Morgan Stanley at +41%, Wells Fargo at +21%, Citigroup at +14% and Bank of America at +10%.
Prime brokerage drove the gains. Goldman's equities financing revenue hit a record $3.37 billion, up 96%. That's the business of lending hedge funds money and securities to make their bets.

Bond desks went the other way. JPMorgan's fixed income markets revenue fell 4%, Morgan Stanley's dropped 7% and Bank of America's slid 17%, which the bank blamed on an 85-basis-point jump in rates during the quarter.
Bank trading revenue now leans heavily on hedge fund leverage and rising stock prices. As long as stocks keep climbing, the trade works.

SK Square stock: Goldman Sachs weighs TMAP control deal
sum: Goldman Sachs is discussing the purchase of a controlling stake in TMAP Mobility from SK Square, according to The Korea JoongAng Daily. The report was published on Friday, October 30, 2026, and said the parties were aiming to complete a transaction by the end of the year.

SK Square is TMAP Mobility's largest shareholder. Goldman Sachs is considering an investment of 700 billion to 800 billion Korean won for a 60 percent to 70 percent stake, while SK Square is weighing whether to retain part of its holding. The company has not announced final transaction terms.

The potential sale is part of SK Square's broader portfolio restructuring, according to the report. The investment company has been divesting noncore assets while concentrating resources on artificial intelligence and semiconductors. It previously sold digital advertising firm Incross to SK Networks and app marketplace One Store to Nexters, as reported by The Korea JoongAng Daily.

sum: Concerns around domestic growth, commodity volatility, and overall geopolitical tension have pushed investors in Indian markets into a wait-and-see mode after equity declines earlier this year. While such caution is understandable, similar periods of discomfort have, in the past, often gone on to become rewarding entry points for long-term investment into India, according to Goldman Sachs Asset Management.

In crises that emerged over the past three decades, Indian equities have rebounded after an initial period of stress, write Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s Aman Batra, head of India equities, and Basak Yavuz, co-chief investment officer of fundamental equity and head of emerging markets equities. We spoke to Batra and Yavuz about their expectations for Indian equities.

The playbook is not very different from what we have seen in previous geopolitical crises. We see a depreciation of the rupee, a flight of capital back to US dollar assets, spiking energy costs, and a correction in the equity markets. The quarter ending in March turned out to be, for Indian markets, one of their worst quarters in recent years, comparable to the kind of corrections we saw during the Great Financial Crisis in 2008 or during the outbreak of Covid-19.

Eventually, energy prices cool down, and after absorbing the increased cost of imported energy, India’s economic growth and corporate earnings both bounce back to their longer-term trend—or, as economists like to call it, their potential growth trajectory. At that point, investors recognize the resilience in earnings and begin returning to the markets as the geopolitical crisis passes. As a result, such crises have often turned out to be good points of entry into the Indian markets.

It started, you could say, with the balance-of-payments crisis in the early 1990s, which led to the reforms of economic liberalization in 1991. The “taper tantrum” in 2013, when market volatility ensued after the Federal Reserve announced a slowdown of quantitative easing, led the Indian government to launch a massive cleanup and capitalization of the balance sheets of public-sector banks. The Reserve Bank of India also adopted formal inflation targets.

To be clear, Oppenheimer is not predicting a bear market, but warned the risks of a correction are high. Furthermore, he pointed out, equity valuations are elevated not only in the U.S., which has been true for many years, but every single region around the world shows valuations “above their own longer-term histories.” In other words, stocks are expensive everywhere, and due for a fall.

As far back as 2024, Oppenheimer made a gutsy and prescient call that U.S. stocks were becoming too expensive, and urged investors to diversify internationally. Why Record-High Copper Prices Aren’t Forecast to Last
sum: A surge in the price of copper that began in late 2025 is likely to fade this year, but it may take several months and a key announcement from the US administration for prices to do so, according to Goldman Sachs Research.

Copper prices on the London Metals Exchange (LME) rallied 22% from under $11,000 per tonne at the close of November to a record high of $13,387 on January 6. While Goldman Sachs Research expects the price to remain supported at $13,000 in the first quarter of the year, the team forecasts prices to decline to $11,000 per tonne by the end of the year.

One key driver of the commodity’s price is likely to be a mid-year decision from the US administration on refined copper tariffs, writes Goldman Sachs Research analyst Eoin Dinsmore. Buyers have been stockpiling copper in the US in advance of the expected import tax, creating expectations of temporary scarcity outside of the US.
“We do not expect the price above $13,000 to be sustained,” Dinsmore writes.

Goldman Sachs Research cites three themes as contributing to the recent run-up in prices. For one, copper buyers significantly increased their requests in December to take metal from LME warehouses, confirming the tightness in markets outside the US. The second theme was the anticipation of strong artificial intelligence (AI)-related demand from the construction of data centers, which use copper in cooling and power distribution.

There was also a narrative in markets that US policymaking for the economy was meant to “run it hot,” as copper and riskier assets rallied in the new year. While Goldman Sachs Research expects growth in consumption of US semi-finished copper products, our analysts don’t anticipate this to have a material impact on global demand growth since the US only accounts for 7% of the market.

Goldman Sachs Research’s copper forecast is based on the expectation that the Trump administration will announce a 15% tariff on refined copper by mid-2026. But there’s uncertainty around that outcome as affordability remains a key focus in the lead up to US mid-term elections which could cause the tariff decision to be delayed.

items.t: Goldman Sachs stock split: what’s next for GS shares?
sum: Goldman Sachs’s share price has evolved over time alongside its strategy, earnings performance and market conditions, yet the company remains one of the few major US financial institutions that has never carried out a stock split.

Goldman Sachs (GS) is one of the best-known financial institutions on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Its share price has moved over time in line with the firm’s strategy, earnings performance and broader market conditions. Unlike many large US companies, though, it has never split its primary common stock.
Explore what a stock split is, Goldman Sachs’s approach, and the latest developments in its share structure, earnings and upcoming disclosures.
Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. Share prices are indicative and may differ from live market prices.

A stock split is a corporate action that increases the number of a company’s shares while reducing the price per share by the same proportion. The company’s total market value remains unchanged because each investor’s overall holding retains the same value.

For example, in a 2-for-1 split you’d receive two shares for every one you previously held, and the share price would adjust to around half its prior level. The aim is often to improve perceived accessibility and support liquidity, although a split doesn’t change the underlying fundamentals.

Goldman Sachs has never carried out a stock split on its NYSE-listed common shares (ticker: GS). As of 15 December 2025, there’s no split ratio, no historical split and therefore no 'latest' split to report.

items.t: The US in last place? Check out Goldman Sachs' global stock forecasts for the next decade.
sum: It can be easy to feel like US stock outperformance will continue after three years of a strong bull market, but the music is probably going to stop soon.
After outperforming the rest of the world for years, the US stock market appears to be on track to fall to last place over the next decade, according to Goldman Sachs.

In a note on Tuesday, the bank issued its forecast for annualized equity market returns across the globe. The US market is expected to return 6.5% a year to investors over the next decade, according to analysts, the worst in the world over the next 10-year period.
It also marks a significant deviation from the S&P 500's historical trend, with the benchmark index returning an average of 10% a year over its lifetime.
Valuations for US stocks are some of the highest in the world. That explains part of the "downside" risk facing the US market, a team of analysts led by Peter Oppenheimer said.
The S&P 500 is currently trading at a 12-month forward price-to-earnings multiple of around 21.
Goldman thinks the S&P 500 could see annual returns as low as 3% or as high as 10% over the next decade, depending on whether markets veer toward its upside or downside scenario.
